blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine peso sank past 63.4 per dollar to hit a fresh record low on Thursday, as investors braced for the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ (BSP) next policy move amid persistently high inflation. The local currency opened at 63.31 against the greenback before sliding to an intraday low of 63.47 during morning trading, data from the Bankers Association of the Philippines showed. READ: Peso sets new record low ahead of BSP meet The latest decline breached the previous record low of 63.373 per dollar set in the previous session.
